questions.question: During generation, what information is available to predict token t?
options: The full sequence after its labels are revealed
Only the final token of the completed sequence
The preceding tokens in the sequence
The preceding and future tokens together
questions.explanation: Autoregressive generation estimates P(x_t | x_<t), so the prompt and previously generated tokens are available when choosing token t. Future tokens are not yet known; including them would leak the answer.

questions.question: For position i, which entries are allowed by the causal attention mask?
options: Positions j greater than i only
Every position except i itself
Positions j less than or equal to i
Only the immediately preceding position
questions.explanation: For row i, the causal mask permits j ≤ i, including the current position and the entire prefix. Positions j > i receive negative infinity before softmax and therefore zero probability; allowing only j=i−1 would discard useful earlier context.

questions.question: Given tokens [t1, t2, t3, t4], what input-target shift trains next-token prediction?
options: Input [t2,t3,t4], target [t1,t2,t3]
Input [t1,t2,t3,t4], target [t1,t2,t3,t4]
Input [t1,t3], target [t2,t4]
Input [t1,t2,t3], target [t2,t3,t4]
questions.explanation: Shift the sequence one place: input [t1,t2,t3] is paired with targets [t2,t3,t4]. Each position learns the next token after its current prefix. Reversing input and target order would train predictions from future tokens toward the past.

questions.question: Why can GPT train on all sequence positions in one forward pass but generate serially?
options: Training masks future tokens; inference needs each sampled token next
Training predicts labels without attention; inference adds attention
Training uses one token; inference uses the full sequence
Training uses a decoder; inference switches to an encoder
questions.explanation: The causal attention mask blocks each training position from using future positions, so one pass can compute predictions for all prefixes without leaking their targets. During generation, a sampled token must be appended before it can condition the next prediction, so decoding proceeds serially.

questions.question: A code-completion service must return the most likely next token reproducibly. Which decoding method fits?
options: High-temperature sampling over the full vocabulary
Randomly selecting from the top-k logits
Greedy argmax at each step
Top-p sampling with a broad nucleus
questions.explanation: Greedy decoding takes the argmax at every step, making the same logits yield the same next token and supporting reproducible code completion. Randomly selecting among top-k choices remains sampling and can produce different outputs.

questions.question: A chat response is too repetitive and should become more diverse. Which adjustment is consistent with the lesson’s sampling guidance?
options: Increase temperature while sampling
Replace the causal mask with bidirectional attention
Shift the training targets by two positions
Lower temperature toward greedy decoding
questions.explanation: Temperature rescales logits before sampling; increasing it flattens their softmax distribution, giving lower-probability tokens more chance and increasing variety. Lowering temperature toward zero concentrates on the argmax and moves in the opposite direction.
